title: Recorded commands name commits that do not exist on replay, so they fail there
foundBy: session agent, reading the failed commands in the claude-api-key replay
details:
The live tiers seed the subject repository fresh on every run, and git stamps each commit with the time it was made. The base commit therefore has a new hash on every run, and so has every commit a member makes. The file member.json hands the orchestrator the base hash, and a recorded orchestrator uses it in commands such as `git diff <base> campaign/dev/subject --stat`.

A replay serves those commands verbatim. The commit each one names exists only in the recording's repository, so the command fails with `fatal: bad object` where it succeeded when recorded. The replay counts them as commands that failed here, 9 to 28 per Claude scenario. On 2.1.283 a failed command also changes the request itself, which VCR-043 now tolerates. A failed commit or merge would change what the campaign produced.

A hash is fixed by its content, its parents, its author and committer, and their dates. Fixing the identity and the dates, for the seed and for the members, gives a replay the hashes its recording had.
